subject: Realtime token drought / websocket lapse during peak – Clearwave
messages:
From: Alex Reed <support@clearwave.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Bethany Olsen <bethany.olsen@clearwave.com>
Date: 2027-06-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Realtime delivery failures during morning ramp

Jasmine / team —

We're seeing a sharp spike in websocket disconnects and partial payloads this morning during our 09:00-09:30 PT ramp. Clients intermittently receive only the first few tokens and then the socket either closes with a 502 or the stream goes quiet for ~10-20s before a truncated chunk arrives. This is hitting our triage flows (high priority).

Error patterns: repeated chunked transfer gaps, intermittent 502 from edge (upstream reports: "broken pipe"), and long tail latencies on token emission. Attaching a trimmed server log and a HAR from a failing session.

Impact: our live transcription pipeline drops words, downstream scoring fails, and customers get partial transcripts. Two enterprise customers have filed incidents.

Can you triage and tell us whether this is an infra regression or something in the streaming runtime? We can flip to non-streaming for a short window if needed.

--
Alex Reed
Platform Ops | Clearwave Health
attach: clearwave_stream_errors.log, sample_har_capture.har

- Confirmed receipt of attachments and HAR.
- Repro window matches our telemetry for a throughput spike across the US-west edge cluster at 09:05–09:22.

Temporary mitigations we can apply with your permission:
1) Force this account to non-streaming responses (turn off websocket chunked mode) for 1 hour.
2) Route traffic to a warm dedicated pool to reduce buffering and proxy coalescing.

We'll fetch keepalive/heartbeat traces and have an initial root-cause hypothesis within 90 minutes. Sorry for the interruption — we'll keep you posted.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-26T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime delivery failures during morning ramp

Alex, Vanessa — initial triage details from infra:

Summary (TL;DR): edge proxy buffering + interleaved slow consumer behavior appears to trigger aggressive connection resets in chunked transfer paths. When several long-lived sessions accumulate buffered KV/cache operations, the proxy's downstream socket becomes momentarily unresponsive and the keepalive fails, which the client interprets as a silent stream. That matches your "token drought" symptom.

Evidence:
- Edge logs (excerpt): "upstream write buffer full -> connection reset by peer" across 6 hosts in us-west-2 from 09:06–09:18.
- Token emission timeline shows normal generator throughput inside runtime; drops occur in the edge-to-client hop.

Immediate mitigations (we can apply now if you approve):
A) Toggle Clearwave to non-streaming (safe) — recommended for the next 60m. Command: `account.set_streaming_mode(account_id=DW-4389, streaming=false)`
B) Increase ws keepalive interval and probe threshold on the affected edge nodes to reduce false-positives: set KEEPALIVE=30s, RETRIES=4.
C) Route Clearwave to dedicated pool `dedicated-usw-02` (warm) — will reduce proxy contention.

Longer term fixes:
- Rework edge backpressure: reduce per-socket buffer thresholds to avoid large coalescing windows; instrument per-account buffered bytes and trigger backpressure earlier.
- Provide non-streaming fallbacks and recommended client-side keepalive guidance in onboarding docs.

I'll open RINF-5673 for the backlog changes and assign owners. If you want the temporary toggle, say the word and we'll flip it.

-Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Realtime Runtime | Redwood Inference
